sentences.text: " 1. List revised.

2. Heard Sri Ajay Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Govind Jee Rai,
learned counsel for the first informant and Sri Bade Lal Bind, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.
3.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Rahul Rai, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 155 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 506 IPC and 5G/6 POCSO Act and 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, registered at P.S. Bhawarkol, District Ghazipur.

4. The First Information Report of the present case was lodged on 14.08.2022 by Hewanti against the applicant, Dhanu Yadav and Ravi Jaiswal alleging therein that on 11.8.2022 on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan she had gone to her maternal house.

On 13.08.2022 she returned in the evening after which her daughter aged about 16 years told her that on 12.08.2022 at about 09:00 am the applicant Rahul Rai, co-accused Dhanu Yadav took her and committed rape on her.
She further disclosed that she loved Ravi Jaiswal since 2020 and he established physical relationship with her many times.
She had a fight with Ravi around 2-3 months back and was not on talking terms with him.
Ravi Jaiswal along with his friends got her raped.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that although the first informant has disclosed the age of the victim as 16 years in the First Information Report but the same is incorrect.
It is argued that as per the radiological examination was opined to be about 18 years of age and as such she is a major girl.

It is further argued that co-accused Ravi Jaiswal has been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 24.02.2023 passed in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No. 7620 of 2023 (Ravi Jaiswal Vs. State of U.P. and 3 others).

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Bail Application No. 7620 of 2023 (Ravi Jaiswal Vs. State of U.P. and 3 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Copy of the said order has been produced before the Court which is taken on record.

He has further placed before the Court an order passed by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No. 32824 of 2020 (Sandeep Kumar Mishra Vs. State of U.P.) and while placing para 20 and 21 of the said order has argued that the Court has observed that false implication in sexual offences is on a rise.

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Bail Application No. 32824 of 2020 (Sandeep Kumar Mishra Vs. State of U.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that as such the present case is also a case of false implication and one co-ordinate Bench has observed that in sexual offences false implication is on the rise and the said fact should be considered.

He further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 10 of the affidavit and is in jail since 16.09.2022.
6.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the victim is a minor girl.
As per school records her date of birth is 01.01.2006.

The incident in the matter has taken place of 12.08.2022 and she was aged about 16 Rahul Rai vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177166048/
2 years at the time of the incident.

entities.text: Rahul Rai vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that the victim has supported the prosecution case.

The applicant is named in the First Information Report and in the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. and there is an allegation of his committing rape upon the victim along with co-accused Dhanu Yadav.
It is argued that as such the present case is a case of gang rape.
It is argued that there is no reason for false implication of the applicant and as such the prayer for bail of the applicant be rejected.
7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the present case is a case of gang rape.
The applicant and co-accused Dhanu are stated to have raped her one by one.
In so far as the order of a co-ordinate Bench in the case of Sandeep Kumar Mishra (supra) is concerned, the said observation cannot be followed in every case and cannot be a universal rule.
If there is credible and clinching evidence against the applicant it cannot be said that there is a false implication.
In the present case, there is credible evidence against the applicant.

In so far as the order of Ravi Jaiswal is concerned, although he has been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court but there was no allegation of his committing rape when the applicant and co-accused Dhanu committed rape upon her
. He was stated to be in love affair with the victim and they had broken their relationship earlier.
The victim is a minor girl.
I do not find it a fit case for bail.
8. Considering the totality of the case in particular, nature of evidence available on record, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected."

5. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant- Rahul Rai, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No.
155 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5G/6 POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(V)
S.C./S.T. Act, registered at Police Station- Bhawarkol, District Ghazipur.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that the victim has been examined as P.W.-3 before the trial court and in her examination-in-chief she does not name the applicant but states of her being raped by Dhanu and one other person who was wearing a black gamcha on his face.
She further states that she was in a relationship with Ravi since long on a promise to marry and there was physical relationship between them.

It is further submitted that in so far as the statement of the victim is concerned, in her cross-examination from the side of the applicant she states that she had given two reports at the police station.

Initially a report was given on 13.08.2022 but the first information report was not written on the same and she was stated that since she is a minor the same cannot be written after which on 14.08.2022 another report was given on the basis of which the first information report was lodged in which the name of Rahul Rai was not mentioned but there was a reference of a boy wearing black gamcha.

It is submitted that she states that she does not know the applicant and does not recognize him and it was the S.H.O. concerned who told her that the boy wearing black gamcha Rahul Rai vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177166048/
3 was Rahul and on the said basis name of the applicant was mentioned in the said report.

It is submitted that the same goes to show that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case on the saying of the S.H.O. but without any credible and legal evidence, the copy of the statement of the victim has been placed before the Court which is annexed as Annexure-SA-1 to the 4th supplementary affidavit dated 16.05.2025.

The applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 21 of the affidavit and is in jail since 16.09.2023.
7.

Per contra, learned counsel for the first informant and learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments of learned counsel for the applicant particularly with regard to name of the applicant which was placed on the basis of the statement of the victim.
8. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that this is second bail application of the applicant.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 11.07.2023.
The fresh & new ground in the matter is on the basis of the statement of the victim recorded before the trial court as P.W.-3.
In her examination-in-chief she does not name the applicant but only refers to an accused Dhanu and another accused who was wearing black gamcha on his face committing rape upon her.
In her cross-examination on behalf of the applicant she states that she had given two reports at the police station.

Initially a report was given on 13.08.2022 but no first information report was written on the same and she was stated that since she is a minor the same cannot be written after which on 14.08.2022 another report was given on the basis of which the first information report was lodged in which the name of Rahul Rai was not mentioned but there was a reference of a boy wearing black gamcha.

9. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

10. Let the applicant- Rahul Rai, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

4 presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.
( vi )
The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.

11. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
12.
The bail application is allowed.
13. Pending application (s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
